key_insight: A single diffusion-based model can be made scale-adaptive to perform joint spatial and temporal super-resolution across multiple upscaling factors, enabling transfer across spatial resolutions and frame rates without retraining a new model per scale.
problem_solved: Existing joint spatiotemporal SR methods are typically tied to a single pair of spatial and temporal upscaling factors, which limits reuse across datasets, resolutions, and temporal cadences—especially problematic for climate applications that need flexible upscaling.
method: Scale-adaptive conditioning: parameterize desired spatial and temporal SR factors so the diffusion backbone can be steered to different upscales at inference.
Shared diffusion backbone with progressive spatiotemporal upsampling: iterative denoising/refinement that produces high-fidelity frames while scaling space and time jointly.
Training/inference strategies for cross-scale transferability (e.g., variable-scale training, resampling and time-conditioning) to reuse one model across multiple SR ratios.
impact: Provides a flexible, cost-effective SR solution so practitioners can apply one model to diverse resolution and cadence requirements (e.g., multi-resolution climate datasets or heterogeneous video sources), reducing retraining and deployment complexity.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LR spatiotemporal input → scale-adapter conditioning → shared diffusion backbone → HR frames at variable spatial/temporal scales.
Before/after grid: low-res frames vs. jointly super-resolved spatial+temporal sequence (animated or stepped frames).
Bar/line chart: accuracy or perceptual quality vs. upscaling factor showing model transferability across multiple spatial and temporal ratios.
Icon set: diffusion/noise schedule, scale slider (for spatial & temporal), and a globe or climate-data icon to emphasize application.
paper_title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Max Defez, Filippo Quarenghi, Mathieu Vrac, Stephan Mandt, Tom Beucler
